turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I keep getting these... these nagging thoughts. I'm a designer, and I just constantly worry that I've missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or maybe that I sent the wrong version of a file to a client. And the thing is, even when I look at it and I can see it's probably fine, my mind just keeps circling back to it. It's getting pretty frustrating.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes persistent, intrusive doubts about making mistakes or sending the wrong files that recurrently occupy their mind even when they see everything is fine, matching obsessional pathological doubt.

turns.doctor_question: When you have these nagging thoughts about mistakes, do you find yourself doing something repeatedly—like re-checking the file, re-reading the layout, or asking a colleague to confirm it's correct—to make the worry go away?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. Before I submit any work now, I'll... well, I usually re-open the file. I'll compare the layers to make sure nothing shifted, re-save it, and sometimes I just mentally walk through every single design choice one more time. 

It doesn't take over my whole day or anything like that, but it definitely makes me slower. I just feel a lot less free creatively because I'm spending that extra time doing all that checking.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors and mental acts—such as re-opening files, comparing layers, re-saving, and mentally reviewing design choices—to manage worries about mistakes before submitting work.

turns.doctor_question: Has this need to double-check and worry about mistakes been a lifelong pattern for you, going back to childhood or early adulthood, or is this something that started more recently?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about exactly when it started. I mean, I can't really point to a specific time in my childhood or even early on in my career and say, 'That's when it began.' I just haven't really noticed a specific timeline for it... I only know it's been bothering me enough lately that I felt like I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.

turns.doctor_question: When you notice these thoughts about mistakes, do they feel like unwanted, intrusive thoughts that pop into your head against your will, or do they feel more like your own natural way of thinking and just being a perfectionist?
turns.patient_response: They definitely feel unwanted. It's not like I'm just trying to be a perfectionist and do a good job. Like I said earlier, they just pop up—these nagging thoughts that I've missed a tiny mistake or sent the wrong file. I don't want to be thinking about it. Even when I look at the layout and I know it's fine, the thought just forces its way in and my mind keeps circling back to it against my will. It's not my natural way of thinking at all, it just... happens.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly describes persistent, intrusive thoughts about making mistakes that force their way in against their will and feel completely unwanted, confirming obsessions.
